_meta.purpose: Frozen v1 registry consumed by the 60 base-type authoring partitions. Owns two things: the VALIDATED `class` ladders (seed-contract.md §2), and the legal-implicit slate per role. No magnitudes anywhere in this file (seed-contract.md §3) — rungs, orderings, references and tags only.
designNotes: Every implicit family listed as legal for a role is tier-equal in strength to every other family on that role's slate — same nominal tier band, same op class. This is enforced by construction, not by a number: no family using the `More` operator (atom.bulwark, atom.savagery) appears on any implicit slate anywhere in this file, because a `More` implicit would categorically outclass a `Flat` or `Increased` implicit at the same tier. Those two families are reserved for rolled affixes only.

A family is excluded from every implicit slate below if it cannot bind today, per atom-layer-handoff.md and atom-family-library.md — not silently dropped, but named with its reason so a later module (E12, the channel-extension spec, the status payload work) knows exactly what to re-open. See `excludedFamilies.global` and each role's `excludedForRole`.

Four roles (`ward-array`, `mantle`, `head-guard`, `sense`) have their entire §2.3-named family cluster excluded today, because every one of those clusters is `stat.derived` (elemental_defense, stoicism, padding, stalwart, immunity, precision, keen_edge) or a still-quarantined shield family. Each carries a small stopgap slate drawn from generic, already-bindable families so the role is not unfillable, plus an explicit note that this is temporary.

D35 (2026-09-04, item-ideal.md rarity...base-types module): the 32-family global exclusion list is re-derived against AtomKindRegistry.cs, not copied from v1's designNotes. Fifteen families carried the stale reason 'stat.derived -- quarantined None/None/None (D6)' -- that quarantine ended 2026-09-02 (atom-family-library.md S3.2's own banner: RuntimeSupportMatrix is Full/Full/None, Lawn and Battle both bindable). Those fifteen are lifted from the global list and from every role's excludedForRole, and added back to legalFamilies wherever they were excluded for a specific role. atom.susceptibility stays excluded (zero readers, a different reason). Five roles were on a full stopgap slate for this reason (ward-array, mantle, head-guard, sense, footing); three more had a partial exclusion lifted (armament-primary, manipulator, standard).

registryVersion 5 (D11 clause 1, 2026-09-12): each role carries legalFamiliesByFrame, splitting the role's legal slate into a humanoid set and a plant set so the two frames draw DISJOINT implicit families. Rule (owner, Option C): semantic where the role has both a burst-signed and a sustain-signed family (humanoid = burst/offence, plant = sustain/defence); a deterministic half-split on the sorted slate for a single-sided role, since a role whose whole slate is one axis has no semantic split. legalFamilies stays as the union for readers that only need membership. D11 widened (item-ideal 2f.2) requires the preference be CORRELATED across roles, which is why humanoid is burst and plant is sustain in every block, never role-by-role.

armour.rungCountRationale: Four rungs matches the item-level band structure already frozen at four bands (ssot-item-categories.md §5.3/§D), so a class rung and a band rung are the same granularity. Fewer than four collapses two of the nine armour-bearing roles' base types into indistinguishable weight classes; more than four would give an item-level band nothing new to say once the class ladder already outran it.

humanoid.identity: Spun and quilted cloth — cheap, quick to move in, and the first thing anyone wears.
Cured leather and boiled hide, flexible enough for a scout and tough enough for a soldier.
Overlapping metal or horn scale, articulated for motion without giving up coverage.
Forged plate, rigid and total — the heaviest thing a body can still move in.

plant.identity: Woven stem-fibre and pith, light enough to sway in the wind it grows in.
A dried outer husk, papery but layered — the plant's first real shell.
Living bark, rough and load-bearing, grown to take a hit and keep standing.
Dense heartwood from the trunk's core, nearly stone and just as slow to give.

weapon.rungCountRationale: Three rungs is the minimum spread that gives armament-primary a real light/medium/ranged-heavy choice, and it matches the frozen weapon class lists in ssot-item-categories.md §5.3 exactly (3 humanoid, 3 plant). Rungs are ordered by combat role, not raw damage number, so the same rung means the same fighting style on both frames.

humanoid.identity: An edged weapon built for reach and speed — the identity slot's fastest option.
A hafted, weighted weapon that trades speed for raw force per swing.
A braced, mounted-feeling armament that throws its damage instead of swinging it.

plant.identity: A thorned, whip-fast vine strike — the plant frame's answer to a blade.
A heavy lobbed seedpod, trading rate of fire for weight per payload.
A braced firing aperture grown for sustained, heavy discharge.

offhand.rungCountRationale: The off-hand's entire mechanical question is binary — does it guard, or does it not (ssot-item-categories.md §5.3: 'guarding classes only'; ssot-equip-slots.md §2.3: 'defensive or amplifying'). Two rungs express exactly that split; a third would invent a category the source documents never describe.

humanoid.identity: A light implement — orb, tome, or wand — that channels rather than blocks.
A braced shield — the answering half's heaviest and only guaranteed-guarding option.

plant.identity: A light secretion vessel — spores or resin — that answers with effect, not mass.
A woven mass of hardened thorn, grown specifically to take the hit the core cannot.

jewel.rungCountRationale: Three rungs echoes the minor-jewel tier cap of 3 already set by ssot-equip-slots.md §2.5 — the class ladder offers exactly as much 'degree' gradation as the tier system above it supports. Ordered by potency/commitment (light claim → bold statement → binding pact), not by mass, since jewelry has no weight-class tradition to borrow.

humanoid.identity: A small marking ring — the lightest, subtlest claim on the jewel budget.
An open wrap of worked metal at the neck or arm, bolder and heavier than a ring.
A bound and weighted seal — the jewel ladder's heaviest, most committed pick.

plant.identity: A released spore capsule — the lightest, most ephemeral claim on the jewel budget.
A stored-energy bulb, bolder and heavier than a loose spore.
A permanently grafted scion — the jewel ladder's heaviest, most committed bond.

standard.rungCountRationale: Two rungs, not four. Commander gear is single-band in v1 — it is not item-level tiered — so a four-rung ladder would have nothing to distinguish. Two rungs give the role a plain field version and a ceremonial one, which is the only distinction the fiction actually supports.

humanoid.identity: Cloth and a pole. Carried because someone has to.
Weighted, gilded, meant to be seen from the back rank.

plant.identity: Green wood bent and bound while it still gives.
Cut from a trunk that outlived three gardens.

standard.addedReason: The commander standard role exists in core.v1.json roles.commanderOnly but had no class ladder and no implicit slate, so a pilot partition could not write a legal class field and emitted none. Found by the pilot, which is what the pilot is for.

armament-primary.identity: What this actor hits with — raw attack, on-hit and on-death riders.

ward-array.identity: The depleting outer layer, spent before HP.

excludedForRole.reason: zombie-only Unity field, not a general frame implicit.
zombie-only Unity field, not a general frame implicit.

armament-secondary.identity: The answering half — reflect, block, parry, or a second armament.

jewel-major.identity: The strongest single non-weapon affix source; a build's signature stat.

manipulator.identity: Rate and follow-through — how often and how hard, not how accurately.

excludedForRole.reason: the role's own §2.3 description names attack interval; excluded globally, pending channel promotion.

head-guard.identity: Resistance to being disabled — crit resist, crit-damage padding, status resist and immunity.

girdle.identity: The resource role — actor resource pools, regen, and economy.

sense.identity: Finding the opening — accuracy and crit rate.

footing.identity: Standing — humanoid evasion/movement/initiative; plant stability/regeneration/resource draw.

excludedForRole.reason: the role's own §2.3 description names movement; excluded globally, pending channel promotion, and zombie-side besides.

infusion.identity: What your hits inflict — the status.apply cluster.

retinue.identity: What else is on the board because of you — spawns, board actions, grid and terrain operations.

jewel-minor-a.identity: Degree, not direction — small, tier-capped, deliberately weak.

jewel-minor-b.identity: Identical twin of jewel-minor-a, and that is the point and the cost.

standard.identity: What the whole squad gains by seeing it. This role binds at match owner-scope, so its atoms reach every ally rather than the wearer.
